summary.plain: A tank of water deep in a Japanese mine, built in 1983 to look for protons decaying. It never saw one, but in February 1987 it caught a handful of neutrinos from a supernova exploding in a nearby galaxy - the first time anyone had detected neutrinos from a star other than the Sun.
summary.technical: Underground water Cherenkov detector in the Kamioka mine (Mozumi), 19 m diameter x 16 m height, 948 20-inch PMTs; originally built to search for proton decay (1983), modified in 1986 to observe solar neutrinos (Kamiokande-II). Detected a burst of neutrinos from SN 1987A (Phys. Rev. Lett. 58, 1490, 1987) and demonstrated that solar neutrinos arrive from the Sun's direction. Predecessor of Super-Kamiokande, built in the same mine.
